name: Omar Silva

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government, and this conversation is confidential. What happens on a normal workday?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a small crew building lines to new solar sites and repairing the older feeders beside them. I studied for a two-year technical diploma, but I still start with the ground survey and the weather. When a new line powers up cleanly, everyone can see what our day bought.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: A gate locked against the plan, a delivery late, or a report waiting when I get home. I use an AI planning assistant every day to sort routes and draft reports, then I check every pole position myself. My partner Leila says I enjoy new tools more than replacing our worn kitchen chairs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my crew the AI planner still earns its place, even if the grand claims fade. It saves me a morning of sorting access notes when we build a new line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am good at this job, but skill is not cash. Leading a power-line crew does not clear my home repair loan. We have less than a month of expenses saved, and the lower rate at this depot makes retirement feel further away than my age suggests.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading the renewable connection crew and using the planning assistant I already use each day. I would put the next two overtime payments straight against our home repair loan, provided the shifts come through.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel steady on the line and worried at the kitchen table. A mild AI future does nothing to shrink that bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much is left on the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: About eleven thousand in our household accounts. My partner Leila and I took it on after the roof leak, and we are paying it down month by month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you add a new AI tool in this picture?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No need. The one I use for plans and report drafts is enough, and I still check its pole positions against the survey.

say: I would tell the crew my existing **AI planner** remains useful even if wider promises fade.
I would say **line construction** still depends on people checking access and pole positions on the ground.
think: Our **repair loan** and less than one month saved keep retirement out of easy reach.
My lower depot **pay rate** worries me more than a limited change in software.
do: Keep leading **connection builds** and check the AI draft against the site survey.
Pay extra **loan principal** from the next two overtime cheques if those shifts come through.
feel: **Anxious** about debt and retirement despite feeling secure in the crew lead role.
S0.quote: Leading a power-line crew does not clear my home repair loan.
fieldNote: His confidence in existing AI tools coexists with a **thin cushion** and lower pay.
He would pay extra loan principal only if **overtime shifts** materialise; current work continues.

steps.text: Keep leading connection builds and checking the existing AI plan on site
Pay extra home repair loan principal from two overtime cheques if shifts come through

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the computer can plan deliveries and answer calls faster, and I would want our crew in the room when the depot changes its workflow. Pole work will still take hands and good judgement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The dispatch office may shrink before any climbing robot appears. If the company uses faster plans to squeeze our field hours, my low savings will not cover a long gap; nearby line jobs are scarce.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would learn the new AI dispatch controls in the first month they are offered and test one real route with the crew. I would also stop the weekly restaurant meal until the loan balance is lower.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I can learn fast, but I cannot learn away an empty pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you test on the route?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the tool’s access times with actual gates and travel on the western feeder. If it sends a truck down a closed farm track, I would log that before a whole crew loses a day.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why cut meals before hours fall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Because less than a month in reserve is too close to the edge. Leila and I can eat at home without calling it a crisis.

say: I would ask that **field crews** help test AI dispatch before new routes become compulsory.
I would remind colleagues that **pole work** still needs trained hands and judgement.
think: Faster office planning could mean fewer **field hours** at a depot with few nearby alternatives.
Our **thin reserve** makes even a short loss of hours a household problem.
do: Learn the new **AI dispatch controls** and test a western feeder route with the crew.
Stop the **weekly restaurant meal** until the repair loan balance falls.
feel: **Anxious** about possible hours cuts despite confidence in learning the new controls.
S1.quote: I cannot learn away an empty pay packet.
fieldNote: He actively volunteers for **AI controls**, a new skill beyond his regular planning assistant.
The restaurant cut responds to a **real cash gap**, not an assumed immediate layoff.

steps.text: Learn new AI dispatch controls and test a western feeder route
Stop weekly restaurant meals until the home repair loan falls

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the depot that thinking AI in 2028 can produce a plan, but a person must check a live line. By the time capable robots reach the poles around 2031, I want our senior crew testing them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would still have field work after 2028, yet I expect the company to stop paying for planning time and cut most overtime. By 2031 the robot could take a larger piece of our work, and I have no savings to wait out a bad transition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the new robot-control training as soon as the depot offers a paid place. If it is offered, I would complete the course while keeping my crew lead shifts; if not, I would apply to utilities outside our area after two reduced rosters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed by the speed, though I have a plan. The loan does not pause while a company decides which crew stays.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you pay for the controls course yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The household cannot fund a private course with less than a month saved, so I need a paid company place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Leila after the second reduced roster?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my partner Leila that I am sending applications beyond our area. We would discuss a move only if an actual job offer paid enough to cover it.

say: I would insist a **qualified person** checks live-line plans made by thinking AI in 2028.
I would ask for senior crews to test **2031 robots** before the depot assigns them field repairs.
think: I expect **planning pay** and most overtime to vanish before robots take a larger share of pole work.
Our **loan** and tiny reserve make a prolonged gap hard to absorb.
do: Complete **paid robot-control training** if the depot offers a funded place.
Apply to **outside-area utilities** after two reduced rosters if no funded training place appears.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely income loss and the short funding window, while holding a conditional plan.
S2.quote: The loan does not pause while a company decides which crew stays.
fieldNote: He treats training as viable only with **company pay** and a funded place.
A search beyond the area follows **two reduced rosters** only if that training option fails.

steps.text: Complete paid robot-control training if the depot offers a funded place
Apply to outside-area utilities after two reduced rosters if funded training is unavailable

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us put new equipment through rain, bad access and a real outage before robots take field work in 2034. I would volunteer to lead that testing if the company pays us for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI arrives in 2031, when I would be sixty three. The robots come later, but I cannot assume I will have retired by then because the loan and thin savings may keep me earning.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my crew lead job and ask for one paid day a month to learn the robot controls during the company trial, if it begins. I would also increase our loan payment by a fixed amount from my regular wage once Leila and I have checked the food and power bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but five years is room to build an answer. I could become the person who spots the failure before it strands a truck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much extra could you pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Perhaps fifty a month, but I will not promise it until Leila and I finish the household figures. I will not cut the power payment to make a tidy loan chart.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire before the robot date?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on present numbers. I hope to work less eventually, but I need actual savings before moving retirement forward.

say: I would volunteer for **paid field trials** before 2034 robots are trusted on outages.
I would ask the company to test **rain and poor access**, not only easy demonstration sites.
think: The **loan** may keep me in paid field work when the 2034 robots arrive.
Five years gives me time to develop a **testing role** if the company funds it.
do: Keep **crew lead shifts** while the depot still has connection work.
Learn **robot controls** one paid day monthly if the company offers a trial.
Increase **monthly loan payments** from regular wages only after checking bills with Leila.
feel: **Anxious** about prolonged income exposure, with a plausible paid role to seek.
S3.quote: I will not cut the power payment to make a tidy loan chart.
fieldNote: He is skilled and adaptable, yet his **retirement horizon** remains financially uncertain.
The proposed extra debt payment and trial role both have explicit **funding conditions**.

steps.text: Keep leading connection shifts while the depot has field work
Learn robot controls one paid day monthly if the company offers a trial
Increase monthly loan payments from wages only after checking bills with Leila

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew we have a decade to put safety rules around thinking AI and then robots. A rushed power-line robot trial would be a choice, not a deadline forced on us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty eight when thinking AI arrives in 2036, and hands-on robots come around 2039. I hope the loan is gone and I have stopped climbing by then, but less than a month in reserve means I cannot call that certain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep working this first year and pay the repair loan from wages on our usual schedule. I would meet Leila with the bank statements each quarter and choose a retirement date only when our savings can carry the bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the bills now, though less frightened by the distant machines. The timetable is long, but the bills are here now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you stop working sooner because of this card?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I want a real cushion before I leave, and ten years of warning gives me time to build one. The card has not brought the date forward.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would help the younger crew?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want the company to publish its robot trial results and keep paid training open. A young lineworker should not have to guess whether a course leads to work.

say: I would press for **safety rules** before the 2036 thinking systems and 2039 robots reach line work.
I would ask the company to publish **field trial results** and offer paid training to younger workers.
think: I hope to stop climbing before **2036**, but current savings do not secure that date.
The present **household bills** matter more immediately than a machine arriving in a decade.
do: Keep **crew lead work** during the first year and follow the existing loan payment schedule.
Review **bank statements** with Leila quarterly before choosing an affordable retirement date.
feel: **Uneasy** about distant work changes, with today’s debt still pressing.
S4.quote: A rushed power-line robot trial would be a choice, not a deadline forced on us.
fieldNote: The long horizon reduces machine urgency but leaves his **current financial risk** in place.
Quarterly reviews are preparation; he does not claim a funded **early exit**.

steps.text: Keep leading connection work and making scheduled home repair loan payments

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because office time could stop paying before robots are ready and I have a home repair loan with almost no reserve. A funded controls place and clear field staffing dates would help me decide whether to stay or seek a utility farther away.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the training is paid while we take it. A course place without wages is not an option for my household.

headlineQuote: A course place without wages is not an option for my household.
portrait: **Omar**, 58, is a highly skilled crew lead with a technical diploma who builds and repairs utility lines.
His **low pay**, repair loan, tiny reserve and few nearby jobs make even AI Plateau financially tense.
He uses **AI daily** already and would learn new controls when training is funded and paid.
The **2028 case** most threatens income before hands-on robots arrive, prompting a conditional search outside the area.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove planning pay and overtime before robots reach his field work.
whatWouldHelp: A funded, paid **controls place** and clear field staffing dates would help him choose his next move.
